newsitem.title: USA: Venture sees Q4 charge, net loss.
newsitem.headline: Venture sees Q4 charge, net loss.

text.p: Venture Stores Inc said it expects to take a pre-tax charge of about $50.0 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 and said the charge likely will result in a net loss for the quarter in the range of $40.8 million to $48.1 million, or $2.24 to $2.64 a share.
This compares with net earnings of $12.6 million or $0.73 a share in the 1995 fourth quarter. The year ago earnings included non-recurring pre-tax charges of $20.8 million or $0.78 a share.

Venture said sales for the five weeks ended December 28 were $274.9 million, down 15 percent from December 1995 sales of $323.4 million. Same-store sales for December fell 13.5 percent, the company said. Same-store sales for the combined November and December fiscal months fell 19.1 percent, the retailer said.

Year-to-date sales for the 48 weeks ended December 28 were $1.41 billion, down 23.5 percent from $1.84 billion for the same period in 1995. Same-store sales for the year-to-date period declined 20.8 percent, Venture said.

"Our comparable store sales gap has begun to narrow as we start the third phase of repositioning Venture as a family value retailer," said chief executive Robert Wildrick. "In addition, our margin before non-recurring charges increased to 25.6 percent in December 1996 from 23.0 percent during the same month last year, continuing the margin improvements that are central to the success of our repositioning strategy."
Venture also said its lender group has waived the fixed-charge coverage ratio provisions for the fourth quarter of 1996 contained in its secured revolving credit facility.
